change.title: pr-2
change.description: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: unsubscribe raises on a missing TopicUser row and bypasses TopicUser.change
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic. Line 107 then raises NoMethodError and the emailed link returns a 500. A row can be missing if the user never visited the topic, for example when they got an email for a mention or reply, or if the row was cleaned up. Separately, `tu.save!` writes the level directly. `TopicUser.change` (app/models/topic_user.rb:77-118) does more for a level change: it creates the row if absent, sets `notifications_changed_at`, sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed`, and publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message (line 112-114). With `save!`, the old `notifications_reason_id` (for example 'watching because you posted') stays in the DB and other open tabs are not told. Fix: call `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, @topic_view.topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead of find_by plus save!.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a non-idempotent toggle, so reload or link prefetch mutes the topic
findings.body: The action lowers the level one step each time it runs: above regular goes to regular, otherwise to muted. The route is a GET that renders a full page. Each page reload, a mail client or security scanner that prefetches the link followed by the user's click, or a browser Back to the page that re-requests it, runs the action again. A watching or tracking user who clicks once becomes regular, and a second hit makes them muted. The page text is the same both times (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`). Make the action idempotent: pick one target state, or compute it only from the level and skip the write if the level is already at or below the target. A confirm step that the user submits as a POST also fixes it.

findings.title: State change on a GET route with no CSRF protection
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes the logged-in user's notification level on a plain GET. It is routed with `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (line 32) and has no CSRF check, because Rails does not verify GET requests. Any page, or any post image URL that points at `/t/<id>/unsubscribe`, makes a logged-in viewer's browser mute or lower notifications for that topic. I did not check whether this version proxies or filters image URLs in posts. Mail scanners that pre-fetch links do the same, see the idempotency finding. Existing code changes the level through `POST /t/:id/notifications` (the `set_notifications` action, which is in the ensure_logged_in list at line 18). The page could render a confirmation and send that request.

findings.title: JSON request with mismatched slug is redirected to the HTML URL
findings.body: `show` goes through `redirect_to_correct_topic`, which keeps `.json` (line 454). The new redirect goes to `unsubscribe_url`, which never carries the format. A request to `/t/wrong-slug/1/unsubscribe.json` is therefore redirected to the HTML URL. The redirect is also a 301, which browsers cache, for a URL that changes state. It is harmless for the mail link itself, so I rate this low.

findings.title: Property name misspelled: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: `stopNotificiationsText` has a transposed 'i'. It is spelled the same way in `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3`, so it works, but anyone who tries the correct spelling gets an empty binding. Rename it in both files to `stopNotificationsText`.

findings.title: No tests for the unsubscribe action, routes, or email link
findings.body: The PR adds a state-changing controller action with a redirect branch, two routes, and a new `unsubscribe_url` template arg. The only spec change is an extra option in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:171-172`, and that spec asserts nothing about the new URL. Nothing covers these cases: the regular/tracking/watching to regular transition, regular to muted, a missing TopicUser, the slug-mismatch and slug-less redirect, the anonymous user, or the unsubscribe URL appearing in the notification email body. `spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb` has no unsubscribe case, and `spec/mailers/user_notifications_spec.rb` does not check the `unsubscribe_url` option.

contracts.action: Email 'unsubscribe from this topic' link opens GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe, which lowers the user's notification level on the server
contracts.equivalent_path: POST /t/:id/notifications (set_notifications) via TopicUser.change, and the client-side TopicDetails.updateNotifications
contracts.before_after: Before: no per-topic unsubscribe in emails. The existing path goes through TopicUser.change, which sets reason and changed_at and publishes MessageBus (app/models/topic_user.rb:87-114). The new path does find_by plus save! with a manual one-step-down toggle, so reason id and changed_at are not updated and no MessageBus message is sent.
contracts.visible_effect: Full-page load renders the topic show template with preloaded JSON (topics_controller.rb:497-500). The Ember topicUnsubscribe route reads that preload through PreloadStore, so the page shows the updated level on the notifications button.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing TopicUser row gives a 500. A reload or prefetch toggles again to muted. An anonymous user gets the ensure_logged_in response and I did not trace whether they return to the link after login.

contracts.action: Ember topicUnsubscribe route loads the topic and shows the notification control
contracts.equivalent_path: Topic route and PostStream.loadTopicView, which use the PreloadStore entry or GET /t/:id.json
contracts.before_after: Same loader. On a full page load it consumes the preloaded topic_<id> that the server put there after changing the level. On client-side transition or Back, PreloadStore is empty, so it calls /t/:id.json, which does not unsubscribe and shows the current state.
contracts.visible_effect: The page shows 'You will stop receiving notifications' text and the topic-notifications-button, with the reason text hidden through afterModel. In-app navigation to this URL shows the text without any change being made.
contracts.failure_mode: If loadTopicView rejects there is no catch, so the route's default error handling applies.

summary: The per-topic unsubscribe link works on the happy path, but the server action has three problems. It raises when the user has no TopicUser row. It is a non-idempotent toggle, so a reload or prefetch mutes the topic. It changes state on a GET with no CSRF protection. It also skips TopicUser.change, so the reason id and MessageBus update are not applied. There are no tests for the new action, and `stopNotificiationsText` is misspelled. The other files in this part (locale strings, email templates, route map, dropdown-button, styles, refactors) have nothing to flag. Nothing was run; this is from reading the code only.
